title: Omer’s kingdom is overthrown
summary: Akish and his friends overthrow Omer’s kingdom. The Lord is merciful to Omer and the children who did not seek his destruction.

explicit_facts.text: Akish and his friends overthrew Omer’s kingdom.
The Lord was merciful to Omer and his sons and daughters who did not seek his destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The overthrow may be shown through Akish’s group taking control of the kingdom.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of the overthrow and the Lord’s visible appearance are not described.

narration.text: they did overthrow the kingdom of Omer.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly; no appearance is described.

title: Omer departs for Ablom
summary: Warned in a dream, Omer departs with his family and household, travels by the hill of Shim and the place where the Nephites were destroyed, and settles at Ablom by the seashore. Jared and his family remain behind.
locations: the place where the Nephites were destroyed

explicit_facts.text: The Lord warned Omer in a dream to depart.
Omer traveled with his family and household to Ablom by the seashore and pitched his tent there; Jared and his family were the exception.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Omer’s household may be shown traveling and pitching tents at Ablom.
unspecified_visual_details: The dream’s imagery and the appearance of the places are not specified.

narration.text: Omer departed out of the land with his family

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The journey includes several locations and is a sequence of travel, not one simultaneous setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent dream imagery or additional travel events.

title: Jared becomes king
summary: Jared is made king through wickedness and gives his daughter to Akish as a wife.

explicit_facts.text: Jared was anointed king by the hand of wickedness.
Jared gave his daughter to Akish as a wife.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The anointing and the marriage arrangement may be represented without adding ceremony details.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, participants beyond those named, and any ceremony details are unspecified.

narration.text: Jared was anointed king over the people

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a wedding ceremony or additional attendees.

title: Jared is murdered on his throne
summary: Jared was murdered while seated on his throne, giving audience to his people.
characters: Unnamed people giving audience to Jared
Unnamed people to whom Akish had applied
locations: At Jared’s throne; the surrounding setting is unspecified

explicit_facts.text: Jared sat upon his throne, giving audience to his people.
Those to whom Akish had applied obtained his father-in-law’s head.
Jared was murdered upon his throne.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jared can be shown seated on a throne with people present for the audience.
The attack can be shown without depicting injuries or its unspecified means.
unspecified_visual_details: The throne’s surroundings, the attackers’ appearances, and the means of murder are unspecified.

narration.text: Jared was murdered upon his throne

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Akish’s appeal preceded the murder; his reign followed it. Neither is depicted as simultaneous with the murder.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Akish at the murder or show his subsequent reign in this scene.
Do not invent a weapon, a throne room, dialogue, gore, or a visible severed head.

title: Akish’s son dies in prison
summary: Akish, jealous of his son, imprisons him and gives him little or no food until he dies. The dead son’s brother Nimrah becomes angry with their father.

explicit_facts.text: Akish imprisoned his son and kept him on little or no food until he died.
Nimrah was angry with his father because of what he had done to Nimrah’s brother.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The imprisonment may be shown with Akish’s son inside a prison.
unspecified_visual_details: The prison’s appearance and the son’s physical condition are unspecified.

narration.text: he shut him up in prison

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nimrah’s anger is reported after his brother’s death; do not imply he is present in the prison moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the death or starvation in graphic detail.

title: Nimrah flees to Omer
summary: Nimrah gathers a small number of men, flees the land, and goes to dwell with Omer.

explicit_facts.text: Nimrah gathered a small number of men and fled the land to dwell with Omer.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nimrah and the men may be shown traveling toward Omer.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and the appearance of Omer’s dwelling are not stated.

narration.text: came over and dwelt with Omer.

prohibited_inventions: Do not add motives beyond the reported anger in Ether 9:8.

title: Akish’s sons draw away the people
summary: Akish’s sons win the hearts of the people despite having sworn to him to do iniquity as he desired. The sons offer money to the people and draw most of them after themselves.

explicit_facts.text: Akish begat other sons, who won the hearts of the people despite having sworn to do iniquity as he desired.
The people of Akish desired gain, and Akish desired power.
Akish’s sons offered the people money and drew most of them after themselves.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons may be shown offering money to people.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the sons’ appearances, and the manner of the offer are unspecified.

narration.text: the sons of Akish did offer them money

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the people accepting money or invent spoken offers, named followers, or additional motives.

title: War among Akish’s house
summary: War between Akish’s sons and Akish lasts many years and destroys nearly all the kingdom’s people, except thirty souls and those who fled with Omer’s household.

explicit_facts.text: War between Akish’s sons and Akish lasted many years.
Nearly all the kingdom’s people were destroyed; thirty souls and those who fled with Omer’s household remained.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The war may be represented through non-graphic conflict.
unspecified_visual_details: The battles, combatants’ appearance, and manner of destruction are not specified.

narration.text: there began to be a war

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The many-year conflict and its outcome are summarized, not a single dated battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore or invent a particular battle.

title: Omer is restored
summary: Omer is restored to his land of inheritance. In old age he begets Emer and anoints him king.

explicit_facts.text: Omer was restored to his land of inheritance.
Omer begat Emer in his old age and anointed him king.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Omer and Emer may be shown together at the anointing.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of restoration and details of the anointing are unspecified.

narration.text: Omer began to be old

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Restoration and the later anointing are separate events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict them as occurring simultaneously.

title: Emer succeeds Omer
summary: After anointing Emer, Omer sees two years of peace and dies after many days of sorrow. Emer reigns in his stead.

explicit_facts.text: Omer saw peace for two years after anointing Emer and then died after many days full of sorrow.
Emer reigned in Omer’s stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A transition of rule from Omer to Emer may be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The circumstances of Omer’s death and Emer’s accession are unspecified.

narration.text: Emer did reign in his stead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The two years of peace precede Omer’s death; do not combine them with the accession as one instant.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a deathbed scene or ceremony.

title: Emer’s household prospers
summary: Under Emer, the land’s curse begins to be taken away and his house prospers, becoming strong and rich. They have many crops, valuable goods, livestock, horses, asses, elephants, cureloms, and cumoms.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord began again to take the curse from the land; Emer’s house prospered and became strong and rich over sixty-two years.
They had fruit, grain, silks, fine linen, gold, silver, precious things, livestock, horses, asses, elephants, cureloms, and cumoms.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Crops, goods, and the listed animals may be shown as signs of prosperity.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s visible appearance, the animals’ exact forms beyond their names, and the setting’s design are unspecified.

narration.text: the house of Emer did prosper exceedingly

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent an appearance for the Lord or for unfamiliar animals.

title: A warning concerning the land
summary: The Lord blesses the choice land and commands that its possessor serve the Lord, warning of destruction and wrath if the people ripen in iniquity.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord blessed the choice land and commanded that whoever possessed it should possess it unto the Lord or be destroyed when ripened in iniquity.
The Lord declares, “I will pour out the fulness of my wrath.”

reasonable_visual_inferences: The land may be depicted as a landscape accompanying off-screen narration.
unspecified_visual_details: No divine appearance or particular landscape features are stated.

narration.text: I will pour out the fulness of my wrath.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a reported command and warning, not a narrated visible divine event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict divine wrath as a literal visible event.

title: Emer anoints Coriantum
summary: Emer judges righteously, has many children including Coriantum, and anoints him to reign. Emer lives four more years, sees peace, sees the Son of Righteousness, rejoices, and dies in peace.

explicit_facts.text: Emer executed judgment in righteousness, had many sons and daughters, and anointed Coriantum to reign.
Emer lived four years after the anointing, saw peace and the Son of Righteousness, rejoiced, and died in peace.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The anointing may be shown as a separate moment from Emer’s later vision and death.
unspecified_visual_details: The Son of Righteousness’s appearance is not described.

narration.text: he even saw the Son of Righteousness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text reports Emer’s vision but does not describe what the Son of Righteousness looks like.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray an appearance for the Son of Righteousness.

title: Coriantum builds cities
summary: Coriantum follows his father’s example, builds many mighty cities, and administers good to his people. He remains without children until exceedingly old.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantum built many mighty cities and administered good to his people.
He had no children until exceedingly old.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A city under construction may illustrate the building of cities.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities’ designs and the timing of each event are unspecified.

narration.text: did build many mighty cities

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific city or child not mentioned.

title: Coriantum takes a wife in old age
summary: In his old age, Coriantum took a young maid to wife.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantum took a young maid to wife in his old age.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantum and the young maid may be shown together without depicting a specific ceremony.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, clothing, and surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: Coriantum took to wife, in his old age, a young maid

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wife's death in Ether 9:24 and Com's succession and reign in Ether 9:25 are separate events, not depicted in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the wife's death, Coriantum's children, or Com's reign as occurring at this moment.
Do not invent a ceremony, location, dialogue, or identities for unnamed people.

title: Heth seizes the throne
summary: As the people spread across the land and wickedness grows, Heth embraces old secret plans to destroy his father. He dethrones and kills his father with his own sword, then reigns in his stead.

explicit_facts.text: The people spread over the land, wickedness increased, and Heth embraced secret plans to destroy his father.
Heth slew his father with his own sword, dethroned him, and reigned in his stead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The killing may be depicted as non-graphic action with the sword.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise setting and circumstances of the killing are not described.

narration.text: he did reign in his stead.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Prophets warn the people
summary: Prophets call the people to repentance and warn of a curse and famine if they do not prepare the way of the Lord. The people reject them; some are cast into pits and left to perish, by Heth’s command.

explicit_facts.text: Prophets cried repentance and warned of a curse and great famine if the people did not repent.
The people rejected the prophets; some were cast into pits and left to perish, according to Heth’s command.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Prophets may be shown addressing people; those cast into pits may be shown in a separate moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The prophets’ words beyond the reported warning, their identities, and the pits’ appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: they must prepare the way of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning and the persecution are separate moments; do not depict them as simultaneous.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named prophets or additional speech.

title: Famine and poisonous serpents
summary: A great dearth comes upon the land; with no rain, inhabitants are rapidly destroyed. Poisonous serpents poison many people, and flocks flee toward the south country called Zarahemla by the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: A great dearth came; no rain fell, and inhabitants were destroyed rapidly.
Poisonous serpents poisoned many people, and flocks fled southward toward the country called Zarahemla by the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Dry land, serpents, and fleeing flocks may illustrate the reported conditions.
unspecified_visual_details: The serpents’ appearance and the landscape are unspecified.

narration.text: there was no rain upon the face of the earth.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The dearth and the serpents’ arrival are distinct events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show graphic poison effects or identify the inhabitants with a named group.

title: Flocks flee south
summary: Some flocks perish on the way and some reach the south. The serpents cease pursuing them and hedge up the way, so anyone attempting to pass might fall by the serpents.

explicit_facts.text: Many flocks perished along the way, while some fled into the south country.
The serpents pursued no more but hedged up the way so those attempting to pass might fall by them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A route blocked by serpents may illustrate the barrier described.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, number of animals, and serpents’ appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: the serpents that they should pursue them no more

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text describes the serpents as blocking passage; avoid adding supernatural visual effects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore or invent a miraculous appearance for the serpents.

title: The people repent
summary: The people follow the beasts’ course and eat the carcasses left along the way. Seeing they must perish, they repent of their iniquities and cry to the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The people followed the beasts’ course and devoured the carcasses of those that fell along the way.
When the people saw they must perish, they repented of their iniquities and cried to the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown praying or crying out, without portraying the Lord.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities and the appearance of the carcasses are unspecified.

narration.text: they began to repent of their iniquities

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Eating the carcasses and later repentance are separate moments.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict graphic carcasses or invent the people’s spoken prayer.

title: Rain and relief from famine
summary: After the people humble themselves, the Lord sends rain. The people revive, fruit grows in the north and surrounding countries, and the Lord preserves them from famine.

explicit_facts.text: After the people humbled themselves, the Lord sent rain and they began to revive.
Fruit began to grow in the north countries and surrounding countries, and the Lord preserved the people from famine.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Rain and renewed fruit may visually represent relief and revival.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible appearance of the Lord is described.

narration.text: he did send rain upon the face of the earth

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord as visibly appearing.
